summary: A conversational interview/podcast with LighthouseAI about their migration to Redwood Inference for production LLM features. Focus on why they picked Redwood, measurable improvements (latency down, cost per request down, reliability gains), and a couple of human stories about shipping the recommender feature faster. Looks like the customer is open to a short highlight clip and a written quote. Next steps: send clip and quote for approval, schedule a follow-up for joint blog planning.

transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, welcome — thanks so much for joining. We're recording this as a customer vignette, totally casual, we'll capture a few soundbites and then Evan will take care of editing.
[00:16] Alex (Lighthouse): Sounds great. Happy to share the story, appreciate you having us.
[00:22] Evan (Producer): quick note — we'll send a waiver after, any redactions just ping us.
[00:28] Priya (Lighthouse): Thanks. I'll be mindful.
[00:31] Samira: Maybe start with a quick lightning intro — Alex, what does LighthouseAI do?
[00:36] Alex: Sure, so Lighthouse builds personalized discovery for e-commerce sites — uh, we do product recommender, search rerank, and a couple of creative generation touch points. We moved to LLM features last year.
[00:47] Carlos: and we ship it as part of checkout and browses flows, so latency matters a lot.
[00:52] Samira: Got it. When did you first evaluate Redwood?
[00:56] Priya: We started a POC around Sep 2024. We were evaluating a few options — MajorCloud AI, our in-house stack using Triton and some custom batching, and Redwood.
[01:08] Marta (Redwood SE): Curious — what were the deal-breakers for in-house?
[01:11] Priya: Ops overhead mainly. Our infra team spent weeks tuning batching and kernel selection, and it was brittle — when traffic spikey would spike the latency would explode. We needed a predictable runtime.
[01:22] Alex: Also the kv cache stuff — we weren't getting good cache hits with our homegrown approach, we were losing prefetched context, so cost leaked.
[01:31] Samira: Nice, and what made Redwood stand out?
[01:34] Alex: The unified serving across hosted and private, the ability to run in our VPC, and the smart routing features. The demo where you showed canary rollouts and automatic fallback sealed it for us — we didn't want full ownership of every kernel.
[01:46] Priya: And the batching/caching recommendations from Redwood Optimize were surprisingly practical. We implemented the prefix caching suggestion and saw immediate change.
[01:55] [00:60] Carlos: quick question — the numbers, what moved?
[02:00] Alex: Before Redwood our p95 latency on rerank was 420ms on average; after moving to Redwood Dedicated in our region we regularly saw p95 around 110–130ms. Token cost dropped ~32% once we enabled prefix caching and optimized batch windows.
[02:16] Samira: That's a great stat, can we get permission to put that in the case study?
[02:19] Alex: Yes, that number's fine.
[02:21] Evan: (quiet) We'll pull a clean quote after — maybe an edited "p95 down 70%" line.
[02:27] Priya: One nuance — we did also change model variants and quantization levels; some of the cost gain came from moving to an 8-bit quantized model for non-critical features.
[02:37] Marta: Right, and we helped with fallbacks so e2e quality stayed stable.
[02:41] [02:45] Tara (Customer Success): From our side we liked the audit logs — compliance was a box we needed to check for enterprise merchants.
[02:50] Samira: Did you integrate with your SSO/SAML and KMS?
[02:54] Priya: Yes, we put Redwood in our private VPC and hooked up KMS for key rotation. SSO was straightforward but the initial sam-el assert config was tricky — small typo turned into an hour of debugging.
[03:06] Alex: (laughs) yeah that was a fun hour.
[03:09] Carlos: Tell me about the rollout — how long to ship the recommender in prod?
[03:12] Priya: From POC to production about 10 weeks — around 3 weeks to prototype on hosted, then dedicated booking and VPC setup took another 4–5 weeks with infra approvals. The Redwood SE team helped with the traffic shaping rules so we could canary to 5% then 25% smoothly.
[03:28] Samira: Do you recall any surprising things during integration?
[03:31] Alex: The most surprising was how the continuous batching improved tail latency during peak times, we expected batching to help throughput but not to reduce the tail that much. The runtime's kernel selection seemed to pick better paths than our tuned Triton config.
[03:45] Marta: There were a few transcription/ops details — small misnames: k-v cash was said in one internal doc (laughs).
[03:51] [03:55] Evan: We're collecting a few personal anecdotes for the podcast — anything human you'd like to share?
[03:59] Carlos: Our growth lead loved that we could launch a "personalized picks" widget for Prime week with zero infra burnout. We actually shipped the widget in 48 hours because inference was stable.
[04:12] Alex: I remember support — your team answered a late night pager and helped triage a region routing blip, that was big for our ops confidence.
[04:20] Samira: Always happy to flex.
[04:22] Priya: One thing — the model catalog you offered helped us pick a smaller open model for A/B tests; having verified perf profiles saved us weeks of benchmarking.
[04:33] Marta: Glad that helped.
[04:35] [04:40] Evan: For the marketing clip, what's a short soundbite you'd be comfortable with — "Redwood cut our p95 latency by 70% and reduced token costs by 32%, letting us ship features faster" — okay to use?
[04:52] Alex: Yep, totally. Use that.
[04:54] Tara: And if you could include a line about security: "integrated with our KMS and SSO" that's helpful.
[04:59] Samira: Great. Any objections from legal or PR?
[05:03] Priya: We'll need to approve the final wording but that's standard.
[05:06] [05:10] Evan: We'll send the waiver and the short clip, by the way do you want a full length audio or just 2-minute highlights?
[05:15] Carlos: Highlights are best for social, full audio for the site.
[05:19] Samira: Switching gear — any tough questions customers asked after launch?
[05:23] Alex: Merchants asked about data residency and retention. We used Redwood's private deployment and configured retention policies; that satisfied them. We did have to explain how caching affected PII handling and what was persisted.
[05:36] Priya: Also we got a few asks about multi-region failover. Redwood's smart routing + fallback to hosted helped there — we had a failover drill and it worked as expected.
[05:46] [05:50] Marta: Anything you wanted improved in the console or observability?
[05:53] Alex: The route-level token-cost breakdown is great; one request — a more visual compare for A/B tests in the console would be nice, like side-by-side latency/cost charts.
[06:04] Samira: Noted — I'll pass that to Product.
[06:07] Evan: For quotes, any preference for attribution? Company name plus title?
[06:10] Alex: "Alex Redding, CTO, LighthouseAI" works.
[06:13] Evan: perfect.
[06:15] [06:20] Carlos: One tiny transcription note — "kv cache" sometimes shows up as K-V cash in our docs, so just be aware when you slice the transcript.
[06:27] Samira: lol we'll clean that.
[06:30] Priya: On the subject of metrics — we also saw error rates fall because Redwood's fallbacks prevented overloaded nodes from dropping requests. Our 5xx rate went from 0.7% to 0.1% at peak.
[06:44] Marta: That's super tangible. Good for the case study.
[06:48] [06:52] Evan: Any competitors or other vendors you'd like us to avoid calling out explicitly in the public piece?
[06:56] Alex: No need to name them. We don't want the piece to feel like a roast. Keep it positive.
[07:01] Samira: Understood. We'll keep the tone product-focused.
[07:05] [07:10] Evan: Quick logistics — Samira will send the clip and a short transcript. You'll have a week to approve the quotes?
[07:17] Priya: One week is fine.
[07:19] Samira: OK — items recap: send clip + waiver, send transcript and quote pulls, schedule blog planning if you want to co-author.
[07:27] Alex: We're in — let's co-author the blog.
[07:30] Carlos: happy to help with conversion numbers.
[07:33] Samira: Awesome. Last question for the podcast: any fun anecdote to close on?
[07:37] Alex: Our head of growth set a ridiculous goal to increase add-to-cart by 8% in 2 weeks — we hit 6.7% and everyone celebrated like we won the world cup.
[07:48] [07:52] Evan: love that. We'll edit that into the human moment.
[07:55] Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[07:58] Priya: Thanks — appreciate it.
[08:00] Evan: End recording.

Notes: timestamps here are approximate — final trim will align audio. Transcription contains minor mis-hearings (k-v cash/k-v cache, sam-el for SAML).
